models.purpose: Categorize nations based on cybersecurity landscape using K-means clustering with Five Elements theory integration.
models.summary: K-means clustering with weighted Gower distance and Five Elements constraint. Partitions nations into 5 clusters aligned with Metal/Wood/Water/Fire/Earth.
objectives: Minimize within-cluster sum of squared distances
Align clusters with Five Elements categories
constraints: Five Elements mutual generation/restriction matrix constraint
Feature weights determined by mutual information
assumptions: Optimal K determined by Elbow Method
strengths: Handles mixed numerical and categorical data via Gower distance
Incorporates domain knowledge through Five Elements constraints
missing_details: Random seed for initialization not specified

details: Random initialization of K cluster centers
Convergence when centers stop changing or max 300 iterations

parameter_estimation.method: Iterative centroid update via mean of assigned points

steps: Assign each point to nearest center (Euclidean distance)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Cluster centers no longer change or change below preset threshold, max 300 iterations.

details: Elbow method confirms K=5 is optimal
identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Cluster separation validated via PCA scatter plot showing distinct groupings.

equation_status.reason: Objective function, distance metrics, and weight optimization formulas explicitly stated.

governing_equations.source_expression: J(K) = sum_i sum_{x in S_i} ||x - C_i||^2
governing_equations.purpose: K-means objective function minimizing within-cluster sum of squared distances
governing_equations.label: K-means objective function minimizing within-cluster sum of squared distances

models.purpose: Establish causal relationship between policy implementation and cybercrime reduction using Difference-in-Differences.
models.summary: Panel data DID regression with interaction effects between policy variables and Five Elements framework components.

variables.definition: Cybercrime rate of country i in year t
Policy variable of country i in year t

objectives: Estimate causal effect of cybersecurity policies on crime rates
constraints: Parallel trends assumption for DID validity
assumptions: Time and individual effects can be eliminated
strengths: Captures causal relationships, not just correlations
limitations: Parallel trends assumption may not hold across all countries
missing_details: Exact country panel composition not specified
Time period of analysis not stated

steps: Classify policies into Five Elements categories
Construct panel data with country-year observations
Run DID regression with policy interaction terms
Visualize results with GeoHeatMap and t-SNE
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Standard OLS convergence for panel regression.

details: Policy classification validated against expert knowledge
identifiability_feasibility.analysis: DID design with interaction terms allows identification of moderating effects.

equation_status.reason: Panel regression and interaction effect formulas stated.

governing_equations.source_expression: Y_it = alpha + beta_1*P_it + beta_2*FE_it + beta_3*P_it*FE_it + epsilon_it
governing_equations.purpose: Interaction effect regression model for policy-Five Elements moderating effects
governing_equations.label: Interaction effect regression model for policy-Five Elements moderating effects

models.purpose: Analyze how national characteristics influence cybercrime through Five Elements mediating pathways using SEM with CFA.
models.summary: Structural Equation Model with measurement model (CFA for Five Elements latent variables) and structural model (national characteristics → Five Elements → cybercrime).
objectives: Model causal pathways from national characteristics through Five Elements to cybercrime
constraints: CR and AVE at acceptable levels
assumptions: Virtual dataset of 30 countries representative of real patterns
Likert scale indicators validly measure latent constructs
validation_refs: CR and AVE at acceptable levels
strengths: Models mediation pathways through latent variables
limitations: Based on virtual (simulated) data, not empirical
Small sample of 30 countries limits generalizability
missing_details: Exact CFA fit statistics not reported

parameter_estimation.method: Maximum likelihood estimation for SEM parameters

steps: Construct measurement model with CFA for Five Elements
Validate factor loadings (>0.65), CR, and AVE
Specify structural paths: national characteristics → Five Elements → cybercrime
Estimate SEM parameters via maximum likelihood
Test interaction effects between Five Elements

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: SEM produces interpretable path coefficients; factor loadings exceed 0.65 threshold.

equation_status.reason: Measurement equations and structural equations explicitly stated.

governing_equations.source_expression: Y_Crime = alpha_Y + gamma_1*M + gamma_2*W + gamma_3*F + gamma_4*E + gamma_5*G + zeta_Y

governing_equations.label: Structural equation for cybercrime as function of Five Elements latent variables
